title: A prospective study on the use of the Inion CPS system from Bricon in the treatment of midface and mandibular fractures and for fracture prophylaxis to avoid subsequent interventions for material removal in adults undergoing oral and maxillofacial surgery. A monocentric study.
summary:
In the context of trauma treatment, non-self-dissolving plates should be compared with self-dissolving plates in bone healing.
In contrast to self-dissolving plates, non-self-dissolving plates require a follow-up procedure to remove the material.
Parameters such as clinical examination, X-ray control and quality of life questionnaires are used for this purpose.
conditions: Fracture of skull and facial bones

interventions.name:
Patients who present to our clinic with midface and mandibular fractures for fracture treatment are examined.

They either decide to use the titanium osteosynthesis plates (non-absorbable) that are otherwise used as standard, control
Or decision to use the osteosynthesis plates of the CPS system from Bricon (resorbable)
